clubs.name: BALLYMAGROARTY YOUTH CLUB
clubs.tried: Register number found: NIC106112 Ballymagroarty Hazelbank Community Partnership (company NI034517), income £334,529, year ending 31 Mar 2025. I read its full FY2025 accounts and directors' report (https://apps.charitycommission.gov.uk/ccni_ar_attachments/0000106112_20250331_CA.pdf, 16 pp; pages 8-16 are scans and I read them as images). The youth club is not named anywhere in them. Its income note (p.10) shows 'Education Authority' £112,567 restricted, but with no project label, so it cannot be tied to the club's EA Local Area award (£115,214.56, 2026-27). NICVA says BHCP runs a 'Youth Outreach Programme' (street-based, funded by Children in Need), which is a different thing from the club. The EA registered-organisations page lists 'Ballymagroarty Youth Club' on its own as a Voluntary Community Organisation, and EA PIP lists 2024-25 and 2025-26 fund the club in its own name. bhcpderry.org does not resolve. Derry Journal and Derry Now return 403. The only club page I found is on Facebook, which needs a login. One search-engine summary said the club 'uses their building'; I could not open its source and treated it as nothing.

clubs.name: Cookstown & Dungannon Women's Aid
clubs.parentName: Causeway and Mid Ulster Women's Aid

evidence.quote: Previous company names ... MID-ULSTER WOMEN'S AID 01 Aug 2013 - 26 Aug 2020 COOKSTOWN & DUNGANNON WOMEN'S AID 23 Apr 1996 - 01 Aug 2013

clubs.relationship: Not a parent and child: it is the same legal entity under a new name. Company NI030137 was Cookstown & Dungannon Women's Aid (1996-2013), then Mid-Ulster Women's Aid (2013-2020), then Causeway and Mid Ulster Women's Aid after merging with Causeway Women's Aid (NIC106208) on 1 Aug 2020. NIC106208's FY2024 report says: 'merged with Mid Ulster Womens Aid on 1st August 2020 and the new merged entity, now known as Causeway & Mid Ulster Womens Aid, took over all of the charitable activities'. The CMUWA FY2025 report (pdf p.6) says: 'Our longstanding role as Accountable body for G-Old Sure Start Partnership came to an end in year. Handover to Barnardo's'. That is the same Sure Start G-old accountable-body role recorded on v237. The v237 record should probably merge into the NIC106888 org, not be shown as its child.

clubs.name: SUNNYLANDS AND WOODBURN YOUTH GROUP
clubs.parentName: Sunnylands & Woodburn Community Development Group (candidate only)
clubs.tried: Read NIC105161's full return for the year ending 30 Jan 2025 (8-page scan, OCR). It names no youth group. The money trail is close: the receipts and payments account shows 'Education Authority Belfast Region' £5,985 in both 2024 and 2025. EA's PIP 2024-25 list names 'SUNNYLANDS AND WOODBURN COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT GROUP' £5,985, and PIP 2026-27 names 'SUNNYLANDS AND WOODBURN YOUTH GROUP' £5,990. The register text lists a 'youth engagement programme' among the group's projects. Together this suggests EA renamed the same recipient, but no document says the youth group is part of the CDG. The EA registered-organisations page has no Sunnylands youth group entry. 'Sunnylands Youth Centre' (Hawthorn Avenue) is a separate youth centre and not evidence either way.

clubs.name: THE VIBE YOUTH CLUB
clubs.parentName: Saintfield Road Congregation of the Presbyterian Church in Ireland (only candidate consistent with the evidence)
clubs.tried: The T:BUC 2025-26 row reads 'THE VIBE YOUTH CLUB LISBURN AND CASTLEREAGH'. The EA registered-organisations page lists 'The Vibe Youth Club | Lisburn and Castlereagh City Council | Voluntary Church Based Organisation'. It lists separately 'Vibe | Armagh City, Banbridge and Craigavon' (= NIC100029, 214 Dundrum Road, Keady), so NIC100029 is ruled out, and VIBE at Five Lamps (Belfast) is ruled out by council. Saintfield Road Presbyterian Church (NIC104268) is at 1 Myrtledene Road, BT8 6GQ, which is Lisburn and Castlereagh (Knockbracken ward, checked via postcodes.io and the project's ni-postcodes.json). Its own site runs 'Junior Vibe Youth Club' (P4-P7) and 'Senior Vibe Youth Club' (Year 8+) (srpc.org.uk/children-young-people/...). That is a church-based club of the right name in the right council, which is still a name and place match only. Neither SRPC's FY2024 accounts and trustees' report (text PDFs; no 'Vibe', T:BUC or EA line) nor its website mentions T:BUC, camps or EA funding. Other registered 'Vibe' names (Vibe Arts & Wellbeing NIC109730 Maghera; Vibe Go Ltd NIC109845 Armagh) are outside L&C.

clubs.name: MID-ULSTER STRONGER TOGETHER (MUST)
clubs.tried: Searched the web again (exact name; MUST + Stronger Together + Mid Ulster towns). Nothing. The full CCNI register CSV has only 'Dunloy Stronger Together' (NIC100130, Causeway Coast & Glens, unrelated). The EA registered-organisations page has no entry. The CWSAN Mid Ulster signposting directory (Sep 2024) lists 'Stronger Together' (the NI ethnic-equality network) and a 'MUST Hostel'. That hostel is the Mid-Ulster & South Tyrone Association for the Single Homeless (NIC100309), an acronym clash and not evidence. The EA T:BUC 2025-26 list remains the only source.
